cleanIntro: Kimber prints two field strips for its 1911s and the one you need depends on what is at the muzzle: a barrel bushing with a recoil spring plug, or a bull barrel with a takedown hole in the guide rod. Both are below, headed. On a Series II keep off the grip safety while the slide comes off — it drives the firing-pin block and the slide will not clear the frame with it squeezed.

steps.title: Magazine out first — this pistol fires without one
steps.action: Press the magazine release behind the trigger on the left side and let the magazine drop free. Do this before you touch the slide: cycling the slide with a loaded magazine still in simply chambers the next round, and a 1911 will fire a chambered round with no magazine present at all.
steps.aside: Remove the magazine by pressing the magazine release button located on the left side of the frame behind the trigger.
steps.quote: This firearm is able to fire both with and without the magazine inserted.
steps.cite: Kimber 1911 Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 50pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in this book; the only year in it is inside a feature note ("California-Specific Models (manufactured beginning in 2024)"), which dates the CONTENT at or after 2024 and is not an edition marker. — OPERATION — Unloading, printed p.42-43

steps.title: Chamber cleared, and let the round fall
steps.action: Grip the slide serrations, pull fully rearward and let the chambered round fall out on its own — do not cup a hand over the ejection port to catch it. Then lock the slide back and look into the chamber and the magazine well before you accept that it is empty.
steps.aside: Do not cover the ejection port with your hand and try to catch the round as it is ejected, as serious injury could result.
steps.quote: In clearing the chamber, allow the ejected round to fall freely out of the firearm, preferably onto a soft, clean surface.
steps.cite: Kimber 1911 Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 50pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in this book; the only year in it is inside a feature note ("California-Specific Models (manufactured beginning in 2024)"), which dates the CONTENT at or after 2024 and is not an edition marker. — OPERATION — Unloading, printed p.42-43

steps.title: ⛔ Which pistol do you have? Bushing, or no bushing
steps.action: Look at the muzzle end. If a separate ring — the barrel bushing — surrounds the barrel and a recoil spring plug sits below it, you have a bushing pistol and you need the supplied bushing wrench. If the barrel emerges alone with no bushing and there is a small hole in the guide rod, you have a bushing-less pistol and you need the supplied takedown tool. Kimber prints two different strips for these and they are not interchangeable — read the one that matches the gun in your hand.
steps.quote: Make certain that firearm is unloaded before beginning disassembly. Otherwise, the firearm may fire when you pull the trigger to release the hammer.
steps.cite: Kimber 1911 Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 50pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in this book; the only year in it is inside a feature note ("California-Specific Models (manufactured beginning in 2024)"), which dates the CONTENT at or after 2024 and is not an edition marker. — OPERATION — Disassembly (Field Stripping): Models with Barrel Bushing, printed p.50-53

steps.title: ⛔ Series II: do NOT squeeze the grip safety while stripping
steps.action: On a Series II the grip safety operates the firing-pin-block push rod. If it is depressed while you pull the slide, the block stays engaged and the slide will not come off — and forcing it damages the pistol, which Kimber says is not covered by warranty. Hold the frame by the trigger guard and dust cover, not by wrapping your hand around the grip.
steps.aside: Do not depress the grip safety when attempting to remove the slide.
steps.quote: Series II pistols: To disassemble, the grip safety must not be engaged.
steps.cite: Kimber 1911 Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 50pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in this book; the only year in it is inside a feature note ("California-Specific Models (manufactured beginning in 2024)"), which dates the CONTENT at or after 2024 and is not an edition marker. — OPERATION — Disassembly (Field Stripping): Models with Barrel Bushing, printed p.50-53

steps.title: BUSHING PISTOLS — plug depressed, bushing clockwise
steps.action: Put the supplied wrench over the recoil spring plug, press it in, and turn the barrel bushing clockwise — toward the right side of the pistol — until the plug and spring come free. Keep the wrench pressed the whole time and keep your face out of line: the plug is the part that leaves at speed if it gets away from you.
steps.aside: Exercise great caution as the recoil spring and plug are under tension and can fly out with enough force to cause serious injury or property damage.
steps.quote: depress the recoil spring plug with the supplied wrench and then turn the barrel bushing clockwise (toward the right side of the pistol) until the recoil spring plug and recoil spring are free.
steps.cite: Kimber 1911 Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 50pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in this book; the only year in it is inside a feature note ("California-Specific Models (manufactured beginning in 2024)"), which dates the CONTENT at or after 2024 and is not an edition marker. — OPERATION — Disassembly (Field Stripping): Models with Barrel Bushing, printed p.50-53

steps.title: BUSHING PISTOLS — plug and spring out, then hammer cocked
steps.action: Ease the plug and recoil spring out of the front of the slide. If the spring does not lift out easily, take the plug only and leave the spring until the slide is off — Kimber offers that order deliberately, and fighting a captive spring at the muzzle is how plugs go missing. Cock the hammer before you go for the slide stop.
steps.aside: Note that the open end of the recoil spring always goes into the plug.
steps.quote: Remove the recoil spring and plug. If the recoil spring does not remove easily, remove the plug and leave the spring for Step 6.
steps.cite: Kimber 1911 Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 50pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in this book; the only year in it is inside a feature note ("California-Specific Models (manufactured beginning in 2024)"), which dates the CONTENT at or after 2024 and is not an edition marker. — OPERATION — Disassembly (Field Stripping): Models with Barrel Bushing, printed p.50-53

steps.title: BUSHING-LESS PISTOLS — capture the spring with the takedown tool
steps.action: Lock the slide back, find the small hole in the recoil spring guide rod and put the supplied takedown tool through it. Then let the slide ease forward until the tool takes the spring's tension. On these pistols the spring is captured by that tool and by nothing else — if it is not seated, everything after this step is a spring under load with nothing holding it.
steps.aside: Exercise great caution as the recoil spring and plug are under tension and can fly out with enough force to cause serious injury, property damage or loss.
steps.quote: Locate the small hole in the recoil spring guide rod and insert the supplied takedown tool into the takedown pin hole.
steps.cite: Kimber 1911 Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 50pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in this book; the only year in it is inside a feature note ("California-Specific Models (manufactured beginning in 2024)"), which dates the CONTENT at or after 2024 and is not an edition marker. — OPERATION — Disassembly (Field Stripping): Models without Barrel Bushing, printed p.57-58

steps.title: Slide stop out — push from the right, pull from the left
steps.action: Line the disassembly notch in the slide up with the slide stop, then push the protruding end of the slide stop pin on the RIGHT side of the frame and draw the stop out from the LEFT. It should come without force; if it fights, the notch is not aligned and levering it will scar the frame.
steps.quote: Holding the slide in that position, push inward on the protruding end of the slide stop pin (on the right side of the slide) and remove the slide stop from the left side.
steps.cite: Kimber 1911 Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 50pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in this book; the only year in it is inside a feature note ("California-Specific Models (manufactured beginning in 2024)"), which dates the CONTENT at or after 2024 and is not an edition marker. — OPERATION — Disassembly (Field Stripping): Models with Barrel Bushing, printed p.50-53

steps.title: Slide forward off the frame
steps.action: Run the slide assembly forward off the frame rails, keeping your hand off the grip safety as it goes. Barrel, spring and guide are still inside it — the slide comes off as an assembly and is stripped on the bench, not on the frame.
steps.aside: Do not depress the grip safety when attempting to remove the slide.
steps.quote: Slide the slide assembly forward and off the frame.
steps.cite: Kimber 1911 Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 50pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in this book; the only year in it is inside a feature note ("California-Specific Models (manufactured beginning in 2024)"), which dates the CONTENT at or after 2024 and is not an edition marker. — OPERATION — Disassembly (Field Stripping): Models with Barrel Bushing, printed p.50-53

steps.title: BUSHING PISTOLS — bushing out the front, guide rod out the back
steps.action: Turn the bushing counter-clockwise with the wrench until its lug lines up with the opening, and lift it out of the front. Then take the full-length guide rod out through the bottom of the slide: lift the guide rod head away from the barrel and withdraw it rearward. If the barrel link is in the way, invert the slide and swing the link fully forward so the rod passes over it.
steps.aside: Remove the full-length recoil spring guide rod from the bottom of the slide by lifting the guide rod head away from the barrel and then withdrawing it towards the rear of the slide.
steps.quote: Using a bushing wrench, turn the barrel bushing counter-clockwise until the lug aligns with the opening and then remove the bushing from the front of the slide.
steps.cite: Kimber 1911 Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 50pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in this book; the only year in it is inside a feature note ("California-Specific Models (manufactured beginning in 2024)"), which dates the CONTENT at or after 2024 and is not an edition marker. — OPERATION — Disassembly (Field Stripping): Models with Barrel Bushing, printed p.50-53

steps.title: BUSHING-LESS PISTOLS — captured spring assembly out the rear
steps.action: With the tool still holding the spring, draw the whole recoil spring and guide assembly out toward the rear of the slide as one captive unit. It stays assembled and stays captured — this is not the moment to see how it comes apart.
steps.quote: Remove the recoil spring guide assembly by withdrawing it toward the rear of the slide.
steps.cite: Kimber 1911 Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 50pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in this book; the only year in it is inside a feature note ("California-Specific Models (manufactured beginning in 2024)"), which dates the CONTENT at or after 2024 and is not an edition marker. — OPERATION — Disassembly (Field Stripping): Models without Barrel Bushing, printed p.57-58

steps.title: Barrel link forward, barrel out the front — strip complete
steps.action: Tip the barrel link forward so it clears the recoil spring tunnel, then slide the barrel out of the front of the slide. That is the whole field strip on either pistol: frame, slide, barrel, recoil parts and — on a bushing gun — the bushing and plug.
steps.aside: The firearm is now disassembled. No further disassembly is required for general cleaning.
steps.quote: Tip the barrel link forward to clear the recoil spring tunnel, then pull the barrel forward and clear of the slide.
steps.cite: Kimber 1911 Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 50pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in this book; the only year in it is inside a feature note ("California-Specific Models (manufactured beginning in 2024)"), which dates the CONTENT at or after 2024 and is not an edition marker. — OPERATION — Disassembly (Field Stripping): Models with Barrel Bushing, printed p.50-53

steps.title: ⛔ Nothing else comes apart, and nothing gets dry-fired
steps.action: Kimber stops the owner here in as many words, and adds two rules people break at the bench: do not drop the hammer with the slide off, and do not dry fire the pistol in that state. Both batter parts that are designed to be supported by the slide.
steps.aside: Do not dry fire your Kimber 1911 pistol while the slide is removed.
steps.quote: Do not disassemble your firearm beyond field stripping outlined in this manual.
steps.cite: Kimber 1911 Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 50pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in this book; the only year in it is inside a feature note ("California-Specific Models (manufactured beginning in 2024)"), which dates the CONTENT at or after 2024 and is not an edition marker. — OPERATION — Disassembly (Field Stripping): Models with Barrel Bushing, printed p.50-53

steps.title: Rod in from the CHAMBER end, every time
steps.action: Always start the cleaning rod at the chamber end and push through to the muzzle — that is the direction that keeps the rod off the crown, and on a 1911 the barrel is out of the gun so there is no excuse not to. Solvent-wet patch first, let it soak a couple of minutes.
steps.quote: Always insert a cleaning rod from the chamber end of the barrel.
steps.cite: Kimber 1911 Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 50pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in this book; the only year in it is inside a feature note ("California-Specific Models (manufactured beginning in 2024)"), which dates the CONTENT at or after 2024 and is not an edition marker. — CARE — Cleaning, printed p.74-75

steps.title: Brush wet, patch dry, repeat until it comes out clean
steps.action: Run a wet bore brush from the chamber out the muzzle several times, then a dry patch, and keep alternating until a patch comes out with nothing on it. Lightly oil the bore afterwards — and put a dry patch through it before you shoot, because oil left standing raises pressure.
steps.aside: Run a dry patch through the barrel before firing to remove oil.
steps.quote: Run a wet bore brush through the chamber end of the barrel and out the muzzle, making several passes.
steps.cite: Kimber 1911 Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 50pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in this book; the only year in it is inside a feature note ("California-Specific Models (manufactured beginning in 2024)"), which dates the CONTENT at or after 2024 and is not an edition marker. — CARE — Cleaning, printed p.74-75

steps.title: Breech face and bearing surfaces — a nylon brush, not steel
steps.action: Wipe every bearing surface on slide and frame, then work the breech face and the extractor with a toothbrush or similar nylon brush. This is where the carbon that causes extraction problems actually lives.
steps.quote: Clean the breech face and all parts (a tooth-brush or similar nylon brush works well).
steps.cite: Kimber 1911 Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 50pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in this book; the only year in it is inside a feature note ("California-Specific Models (manufactured beginning in 2024)"), which dates the CONTENT at or after 2024 and is not an edition marker. — CARE — Cleaning, printed p.74-75

steps.title: Lubricate by the drop, and keep oil OUT of the firing pin channel
steps.action: Kimber counts the drops: three per side on the slide and frame rails, one on the disconnector, two spread across the barrel hood, one on each locking lug, one behind the barrel link, one on the slide stop pin, three spread over the outside of the barrel, one between hammer and frame. Grease is not recommended. And nothing goes into the firing pin channel — oil there slows the pin and causes misfires.
steps.aside: Slide and frame rails; 3 drops on each side.
steps.quote: Do not place lubricant into the firing pin channel as oil there may slow the movement of the firing pin, and can cause a misfire.
steps.cite: Kimber 1911 Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 50pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in this book; the only year in it is inside a feature note ("California-Specific Models (manufactured beginning in 2024)"), which dates the CONTENT at or after 2024 and is not an edition marker. — CARE — Lubrication, printed p.75-76

deepAbsentReason: Kimber publishes no procedure past the field strip for an owner and forbids going further in as many words: "Do not disassemble your firearm beyond field stripping outlined in this manual. Do not manipulate any internal components beyond what you are instructed to do in this manual." It adds that mainspring and firing pin spring replacement — the only scheduled work deeper than the strip — "should be performed by the Kimber factory". There is no deeper published procedure to author, and the manufacturer's DON'T outranks any other source, so the absence is recorded rather than filled from elsewhere.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Rod in from the CHAMBER end, always
Wet patch, soak, wet brush chamber-to-muzzle, dry patch, repeat until clean
Light oil, then a dry patch before shooting

cleaning.name: SLIDE & BREECH FACE
tasks: Nylon brush on the breech face and extractor
Wipe every bearing surface inside the slide
⛔ No oil in the firing pin channel — it slows the pin and causes misfires

cleaning.name: FRAME & RAILS
tasks: 3 drops of oil per side on the rails, 1 on the disconnector, 1 on the slide stop pin
Grease is not recommended; premium oil only

cleaning.name: BARREL, LUGS & LINK
tasks: 2 drops spread across the barrel hood
1 drop on each locking lug, inside the slide and on the barrel
1 drop behind the barrel link; 3 drops spread over the barrel exterior

cleaning.name: RECOIL SPRING — REPLACE ON SCHEDULE
tasks: Custom/Target (5-6"): .45/.40 at 1,500 rounds; 9mm and .38 Super on their own intervals
Ultra (3"): 800 rounds — the shortest interval in the book
⛔ Closed end of the spring goes down the guide rod first, open end to the muzzle

reassembly: Slide upside down; barrel in through the muzzle end with the link forward and clear of the recoil spring tunnel.
BUSHING PISTOLS: bushing in over the barrel with its lug aligned to the tunnel opening, then turned clockwise to about 9 o'clock.
BUSHING PISTOLS: guide rod in from the breech end, contoured edge of the head facing the barrel; recoil spring down the rod CLOSED end first.
BUSHING-LESS PISTOLS: the captured recoil assembly goes in from the breech end, still held by the takedown tool.
Slide onto the frame rails with the hammer cocked — and without touching the grip safety on a Series II.
Bring the slide back until the barrel link lines up with the slide stop hole; look through the hole to confirm it before the pin goes in.
Slide stop in from the left, rotated into place and pushed fully home without scraping the frame.
BUSHING PISTOLS: plug onto the spring, pressed in below the front of the slide, then captured by turning the bushing counter-clockwise.
BUSHING-LESS PISTOLS: lock the slide back to take the load off the takedown tool, then remove the tool.
Safety off, cycle the slide several times, then function check.
fncheck: Reassembled, magazine out, chamber empty, muzzle safe. Cycle the slide by hand several times and feel it run without binding on the bushing or the guide rod. Check the thumb safety engages only with the hammer cocked and that it blocks the trigger; check the grip safety releases the trigger only when the web of your hand depresses it — and on a Series II, that the pistol will not fire with the grip safety released. Anything inconsistent goes to Kimber Product Services rather than the range.
